The gold's javadoc promises the interpreter that refines types from the outcome of a condition with the Closure primitives, such as goog.isDef, recognized when closurePrimitives is set; the variant returns the last link of the chain (append returns the appended link), which does not refine a top-level goog.isDefAndNotNull(x) call. The flag is the only value above the gold that changes the result, and neither value restores the refinement. The convention is pinned outside the gold: ChainableReverseAbstractInterpreter.append ('returning the updated last link'; new X().append(new Y()) 'forms a chain starting with X'), getFirst ('Gets the first link of this chain') and firstPreciserScopeKnowingConditionOutcome ('starting with the first link'), AbstractCompiler.getReverseAbstractInterpreter ('Get an interpreter for type analysis'); the passing tests TypeCheckTest testClosure3 and testClosure1 build the same chain with .append(..).getFirst() and check that goog.isDefAndNotNull(a) and goog.isDef(a) narrow a at the top of a condition; TypeInferenceTest testAssertWithNotIsNull shows the compiler's own interpreter recognizes goog.isNull with closurePass on; ClosureReverseAbstractInterpreterTest testGoogIsDefAndNotNull1 shows the Closure interpreter narrows goog.isDefAndNotNull.
